edges.description: Knockout and rescue establish a role in complex I biogenesis; ND4 association and secondary TMEM126B loss offer partly overlapping mechanistic explanations.
TMEM126A associates with OXA1L, ribosomes and nascent chains; loss impairs their biogenesis. Cargo stalling is inferred from interaction, proteolysis and rescue experiments.
TMEM126B protein levels fall after TMEM126A depletion or knockout; the intermediate regulatory or stability mechanism remains unresolved.
The proposed cargo-insertion defect is coupled to protease-dependent OXA1L fragmentation in TMEM126A-depleted cells and isolated mitochondria.

The inferred insertion defect exposes nascent cargo to iAAA-dependent quality control. YME1L codepletion restores labeled proteins; this does not demonstrate that cleavage of OXA1L itself causes cargo loss.
intermediate_mechanisms: Proteolytic clearance of newly synthesized cargo associated with OXA1L

edges.description: Loss of the ND2-module assembly factor TMEM126B compromises complex I biogenesis; untagged TMEM126B rescues assembly in TMEM126A-null cells.
Reduced abundance of assembled enzyme lowers measured complex I activity, although residual active enzyme remains.

The step from a ubiquitous enzyme deficiency to a cell-type-restricted degeneration is exactly what is not explained for this disease, so the intermediates are recorded as unknown rather than asserted.
Loss of ganglion-cell axons is reflected by optic atrophy on clinical examination; the cited patients were not assessed by retinal histology.
Acuity loss follows from degeneration of the papillomacular bundle that carries central vision, which is the intermediate step.
Same papillomacular-bundle intermediate, measured as a field defect rather than as acuity.
Dyschromatopsia follows from loss of the same central axon population, and is characteristically severe in this disorder.
The retinal nerve fiber layer contains ganglion-cell axons, whose loss is reflected by OCT thinning.
Axonal loss produces the pale optic disc seen on examination.
intermediate_mechanisms: Loss of optic nerve axons and associated tissue remodeling

nodes.description: TMEM126A-deficient HEK293T and HAP1 cells show reduced complex I assembly and activity, with residual active enzyme. Other respiratory complexes were relatively preserved in the 2021 models, whereas the 2024 HEK293 experiments also detected smaller or clone-dependent effects on other OXPHOS complexes. In HAP1 cells, basal respiration and substrate-driven ATP synthesis were preserved, but maximal respiratory capacity and viability under galactose stress were reduced. Patient fibroblast measurements were discordant in the founding families, and these cellular results do not establish uniform ATP depletion in retinal ganglion cells.

nodes.description: TMEM126A loss reduces assembled respiratory complex I. The 2021 HEK293T study found transient association with newly synthesized ND4 and slower ND4 labeling without faster turnover of the labeled pool, supporting an early biogenesis role. A 2024 HEK293 study instead attributed its complex I defect to secondary TMEM126B loss: untagged TMEM126B rescued assembly and activity, whereas C-terminally FLAG-tagged TMEM126B did not. These findings qualify the earlier tagged-paralog rescue experiment and do not establish unconditional non-interchangeability.

nodes.description: TMEM126A interacts with the OXA1L insertase, mitochondrial ribosomes and newly synthesized mitochondrial polypeptides. Loss of this accessory protein is proposed to impede cotranslational membrane insertion and stall cargo at OXA1L. Direct cross-linking establishes nascent-chain association; the chaperone-like insertion role and cargo-stalled state remain mechanistic interpretations of the biochemical experiments.

nodes.description: Newly synthesized mitochondrial proteins are depleted after TMEM126A knockdown or knockout in the 2024 HEK293 study. YME1L codepletion restores labeled products, while mtDNA, mitochondrial RNA and tested ribosomal protein levels are preserved. Untagged TMEM126B rescues complex I but not this nascent-protein defect, distinguishing the two biochemical outcomes. The contribution of this broader proteostasis defect to human optic neuropathy remains unresolved.

His affected siblings did not have this reported complication. Symptoms improved after intravenous immunoglobulin, but the single observation does not establish a TMEM126A-specific immune mechanism or treatment efficacy.

nodes.description: Disease-associated TMEM126A genotypes include predicted truncating alleles and a splice variant with measured exon 2 skipping. The splice change removes the normal translation start from the major transcript; a shorter isoform persists, and complete absence of every functional protein product was not demonstrated. Reported missense alleles require variant-specific interpretation rather than an automatic null classification.

nodes.description: The 2021 D’Angelo study directly tested a TMEM126A-knockout line in addition to its NDUFS3 perturbation models. Respiratory-chain measurements, oxygen consumption and galactose survival support a conditional bioenergetic defect.

The 2021 Formosa study measured complex I assembly, residual activity, pulse-labeled ND4 association and rescue by TMEM126A. The C-terminal FLAG-tagged TMEM126B comparator did not rescue, a construct limitation clarified by the later untagged experiment.

Homozygous in Iraqi siblings in 2019 and in affected members of Chinese family F98 in 2020. The first report explicitly classified it as VUS; the later report argued for pathogenic or likely pathogenic status from segregation, conservation and modeling. These are differing published interpretations without a direct allele-specific functional assay. The Chinese narrative calls the affected pair brothers, whereas its demographic table records one male and one female; sex-specific conclusions are not drawn.

nodes.description: OXA1L undergoes partial proteolytic cleavage after TMEM126A loss. Depletion of YME1L, PARL or SLP2 suppresses this cleavage, whereas AFG3L2 depletion does not. The observed turnover is interpreted as mitochondrial inner-membrane quality control acting on insertion complexes; it is not evidence of complete OXA1L depletion in every knockout condition.
